deep.reconstruction:
Dated 1.1.84, this is a correction-and-supplement sheet in the 1983-84 dossier on systems of pseudo-lines (arrangements of pseudo-lines in the real projective plane). The whole page is crossed out with a green X, which suggests it was superseded. The object (X,K) appears to be a cellular decomposition attached to an arrangement or family of arrangements. K_0 is its 0-skeleton (vertices), X_1 is a 1-dimensional stratum or skeleton, and phi is a map whose preimage carries the union L of the pseudo-line branches. 'Facettes exceptionnelles' are the cells where the arrangement is non-simple, i.e. multiple (more than double) points occur.

(a) Correction of an earlier claim: phi^{-1}(X_1) = L ∪ K_0, not L. Isolated vertices also map into X_1.

(b) Local normal form of an exceptional facet near an exceptional edge, or better near the pair of facets adjacent at an exceptional vertex. The figure shows two faces F and F' between yellow vertical edges, red branches of L, and a horizontal line D through a point a.
- At a multiple vertex s, choose a 'principal branch' delta of L in an exceptional face.
- All the other branches of L through s are then concurrent at a point of ∂F lying on K_0.
- By a 'loi de symétrie' (law of symmetry) the same happens in the neighbouring face ('joint') with equal multiplicity.
- The symmetry law also governs the multiplicities of the double points of L lying on the two ordinary edges incident to a.

(c) Rule for a 'voie privilégiée' (privileged path or route) along the edges of F other than the three marginal ones. For a face bounded by an ordinary edge or an exceptional vertex, the privileged route is the one that is simultaneously convergent and unstable. This is Morse- or flow-like language: stable versus unstable directions of a deformation.

(d) To determine the relative position (the combinatorial type) associated with an exceptional face, one must know the generic arrangement nearby. One takes phi(∂F*), where F* is obtained from F by replacing the critical vertices on the privileged route opposite to F. Equivalently, one modifies the 'exceptional boundary' of L by a path joining the two principal critical points through the interior of F (the dotted line in pen on the figure).

Overall purpose: a local combinatorial and topological description of how non-generic (multiple-point) arrangements sit in the cell structure, and how to read off neighbouring generic types. This is a precursor-type question to the study of the cell structure of spaces of pseudo-line arrangements (flips, triangle moves).
errors: (a) is itself an explicit self-correction of an earlier statement: phi^{-1}(X_1) is L ∪ K_0, not L alone.
The page is crossed out (green X), so its content was presumably revised or superseded on later pages.
Several statements are fragmentary: 'loi de symétrie', 'voie privilégiée' and 'joint' are defined on earlier pages, which are not available. Correctness cannot be fully checked.
In (c) the criterion 'converge et à la fois instable' is not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Local structure of non-simple (multiple-point) cells in a cell decomposition associated with pseudo-line arrangements: choice of a principal branch at a multiple point, with the other branches concurrent at a boundary vertex.
ideas.modern_name: Local structure of strata of non-simple arrangements; triangle flips / Reidemeister-III-type moves in spaces of pseudo-line arrangements (oriented matroid strata, higher Bruhat orders)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956), Goodman–Pollack (1980s), Manin–Schechtman (1989), Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler (Oriented Matroids, 1993)

ideas.what: Privileged route chosen as the convergent-and-unstable direction, used to pass from an exceptional face to a neighbouring generic configuration.
ideas.modern_name: Morse/flow-type resolution of degenerate configurations; choice of adjacent generic chamber
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; standard in stratified Morse theory or oriented matroid mutation arguments

ideas.what: Law of symmetry for multiplicities of double points on the two ordinary edges incident to a vertex.
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial symmetry of local intersection data (no clear modern name)

missed.claim: Grothendieck was developing, in early 1984, a local normal form for exceptional (multiple-point) cells and a rule for recovering adjacent generic types via 'privileged routes'. This is an attempt at a combinatorial-topological description of the stratification of the space of pseudo-line arrangements. Here it appears only as crossed-out technical fragments; the overall programme is documented elsewhere in cote 154.
missed.quote: Pour avoir la position relative correspondante à une face exceptionnelle, il faut connaître la variété générale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is marginal historical interest as an independent approach to the stratification of spaces of pseudo-line arrangements, contemporaneous with or before Manin–Schechtman and Mnëv. There is no self-contained new result on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The page holds local technical corrections in a crossed-out working sheet. It is interesting only as part of Grothendieck's little-known pseudo-line programme; no standalone result here is likely new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Title: the word read 'multiplication' is most likely 'modification' ('Compléments et modification(s) sur les facettes exceptionnelles de (X,K)'). The same word recurs in (d) as 'modification obtenue'.
(b): likely 'au voisinage d'une arête exceptionnelle (ou mieux, de la droite paire des facettes adhérentes à un sommet exceptionnel)'.
(b): likely 'toutes les branches de L en s distinctes de delta sont concourantes en un pt ... de ∂F sur K_0', rather than 'dans les branches ... aux s distinctes'.
(c): likely 'Pour toutes arêtes de F distinctes des trois arêtes marginales ... la voie privilégiée est celle ...'.
(d): 'où F* est l'adhérence de F' is probably 'où F* est déduite de F par remplacement des sommets critiques ...'.
The date in the image could be read as 1.1.83 or 1.1.84; 1.1.84 fits the dossier dates.
